[quote=kalosian_union;60737394]The Foreign Minister was...to put it simply, a hungry person. Being the diplomat to Thyven before the revolution, he was used to many a banquet, both in Thyven and with the royals. When he was offered breakfast, he of course immediately accepted the offer. He ordered whatever he could take and ate pretty much everything. After all, didn't he deserve food after having to endure talking and walking Wikipedia editor?. Once he had determined himself done with his breakfast, he immediately went to complete his actual objective in this country, which was unfortunately not food, which he was now starting to regret not eating more of. But a diplomatic meeting. He navigated through the palace until he could find the Foreign Minister.[/quote]
The older secretaries nodded in approval. A man who eats is a man who knows how to please a host. They served him all the local morning delicacies and anything foreign that was available. With a bit of scrutiny to his reaction to certain foods, both for political double meanings or to plain make sure an item isn't served again. They can trust a man whose heart is in his stomach.

Thankfully Dame Catherine Walker ate in a slowness than matched the Minister's appetite so she had finished her own about ten minutes before he finished his and used the time to prepare before a butler of the palace directed him to the lounging area designated for negotiations.

Wherein a tray of butter layered biscuits, chocolate crackers, and jam tarts awaited alongside some simple cool lemon soda juice for the digestion. Inside Dame Catherine Walker awaited, firm and proper smile, a woman on her late fifties, who immediately greeted him with a polite and plain "Welcome to Eneas, Minister Thorn. I am Dame Catherine Walker, you may call me Minister Walker or Ma'am." She got through the pleasantries quickly.

"Shall we take a seat? We're very much interested in your government in exile and your royals regarding the Matter of Moselle Succession." She began.
